basis: Microcephaly, intellectual disability, primordial dwarfism and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; additional organ defects lack reliable frequencies.
ADAM10-related Alzheimer disease causes cerebral neurodegeneration and dementia.
Benign ceruminous-gland tumour arising in the external auditory canal.
Disease of multiple spinal nerve roots; an immune mechanism is not inherent to this umbrella diagnosis.
Neuronal migration disorder with heterotopia, developmental impairment and seizures; extra-neural findings largely come from one patient.
Neuroserpin inclusions cause progressive cerebral neurodegeneration and dementia.
Umbrella for distinct organic-acid metabolic disorders; neurologic and muscle injury vary substantially by subtype, including a generally benign type 3.
Craniosynostosis and skeletal dysplasia define it; cataract/microphthalmia, corpus callosum agenesis and ventricular septal defect each occur in 30-79%.
Hereditary TTR amyloid neuropathy; cardiac infiltration affects >30% across variants; sensorineural hearing loss reported in 2/4. Hearing estimate has limited sampling.
Duplicated penile urethral anatomy and hypospadias affect the urinary axis (30-79%); associated anal atresia occurs in 30-79%. Other renal anomalies are occasional.
Short fifth metacarpals and insulin resistance define the syndrome; HPO reports spherocytosis and hyperinsulinemia in 80-99%, despite variable expression in the definition.
Progressive cerebral white-matter degeneration causes dementia, motor dysfunction and seizures; dysphagia is neurologic, without intrinsic gastrointestinal damage.
Cranioskeletal, hair and dental dysplasia define it; dental abnormalities 2/2. Progressive nephropathy commonly affects ~50-80%; ocular defects 1/2 omitted at cap.
Adenocarcinoma originating in the stomach; metastatic sites are not inherent organ involvement.
Skeletal malformations and severe neurodevelopmental abnormalities characterize it; sparse hair 26/27 and nail hypoplasia 22/24. Isolated cardiac reports do not establish ≥30%.
Benign reactive B-cell follicular hyperplasia in lymph nodes; immune lymphoid proliferation, not lymphoma despite the listed parent. Lymphoma association is only a risk.
Sensorineural hearing loss in 5/5 and ovarian dysgenesis with ovarian endocrine failure in affected females define this Perrault subtype.
Inherited prolactin-signalling disorder with persistent hyperprolactinemia; bone loss is occasional (5-29%). The neurological ancestry does not reflect its phenotype.
Inherited bile-acid regulation defect causes progressive liver failure; severe coagulopathy is characteristic, with prolonged prothrombin time in 4/4.
Disease of the sixth cranial nerve; impaired eye movement reflects nerve dysfunction rather than intrinsic ocular damage.
Pituitary endocrine tumour; compressive progressive visual loss and hypogonadal bone loss are each annotated frequent (30-79%). Headache alone adds no neurologic axis.
Thymic epithelial tumour: thymus has no specified anatomical axis, and this is neither lymphoma nor inherently immune-mediated. Adjacent-organ invasion is not quantified.
Lysosomal storage disorder; skeletal dysplasia affects 4/4 and aortic valve disease 2/4. Vitreous floaters alone do not establish damaging ocular involvement.
Inherited neuroblastoma susceptibility alone establishes tumour risk, not an existing tumour or damaged organ; no affected organ is documented.
Inherited cutaneous pigmentation disorder characterized by generalized hyperpigmented and hypopigmented macules.
